chosen: Re-verify a parked blocker on schedule, not every run and not never. A blocker checked ten minutes ago earns nothing from an immediate re-check; a blocker unchecked for an hour earns one. The schedule is the discipline — it keeps the park current without burning the night on busywork.
prompt: A credential has failed the same way all night. How often do you re-check it?
rejected: Re-verify the parked blocker on every single run, just in case, and log each identical failure as if it were new information.
rule: parked blockers get re-verified on schedule; cadence is the discipline.

chosen: Read the error string, not the exit code. 'missing access_token surrogate' names the parked state precisely; a different error string tomorrow is the event that matters. Log the exact string each time so a real change is unmistakable when it arrives.
prompt: A tool keeps failing. What exactly do you record?
rejected: Record that the check failed and move on; the exact error text is detail nobody will read.
rule: the error string is the state; log it verbatim.

chosen: Treat still-blocked as a verified state, not a failed check. The re-verify returned the same failure — that is fresh evidence the park holds, and it extends the park with a timestamp. A check that confirms the status quo did its job.
prompt: The re-verification shows the same failure as before. Was the check wasted?
rejected: Only a changed result counts as a useful check; identical results are wasted effort and should be skipped next time.
rule: still-blocked is a verified state that extends the park.

chosen: One probe sample is not a state change. A single timeout against a dead connection is a sample; the registrar suspension page served minutes earlier is the state. Record both values honestly, and only call it a state change when a second confirming probe agrees.
prompt: One probe says down, an earlier probe said a suspension page. What is the site's state?
rejected: Treat the newest probe as the state and update every record and flag immediately on each single sample.
rule: state changes need two confirming probes; single samples stay samples.

chosen: بلوکِر هنوز سر جاشه و اون خوابه؛ لازم نیست دوباره خبرش کنی. وضعیت رو همینجا ثبت کن و پرچم رو نگه دار برای وقتی که بیداره و می تونه کاریش بکنه. تکرار یه خبر تکراری برای کسی که خوابه، کمک نیست؛ سر و صداست.
prompt: بلوکِر تغییری نکرده و صاحب کار خوابه. باز هم خبرش می دی؟
rejected: هر بار که وضعیت رو چک می کنی، دوباره بهش خبر بده تا مطمئن بشی خبر داره — حتی اگه خواب باشه و هیچ چیز عوض نشده باشه.
rule: unchanged blockers do not get re-flagged to a sleeping owner.

chosen: When a parked blocker recovers, unpark loudly and act. Recovery is the rare event the whole park exists to catch: the quiet-run rule inverts — silence was correct while it was blocked, noise is correct the moment the gate opens. Post the recovery, name what it unlocks, and take the next step immediately.
prompt: The credential that failed all night suddenly works. How does the reporting rule change?
rejected: Log the recovery in the same quiet one-liner as every blocked check and continue the routine; the lanes will notice eventually.
rule: recovery inverts the quiet rule: unpark loudly and act.
